title: Review of c26's predator persistence vs arena size: on fresh seed 5, 192^2 replicates (predator gone 104 t after introduction) but 256^2 does not (predator never blooms, at most 1 cell, extinct 56 t after introduction)
summary: labkit runs of the specialist predator world (PRED=1, T_INTRO=200, PSIG=8, DECB=0.002) on fresh seed 5 to t=1200. 192^2: predator 13 cells at t=200-ish bloom, prey 39 -> 3, predator last seen t=304, prey back to 43-47, as reported (90-120 t). 256^2: the planted predator holds at most 1 cell and is gone by t=256 while prey grow to 78 and saturate; no prey-predator cycle. So persistence is not set by arena size alone: whether the introduced predator establishes varies by seed. Weak: one seed per size, and I did not check where the predator was planted relative to the prey.

observations.finding: rerun/L192 (seed 5): predator last seen t=304 (104 t after introduction); rerun/L256 (seed 5): predator max 1 cell, last seen t=256, prey 78

seeds_run.result: 256^2 fail: predator extinct 56 t after introduction, no bloom (claim 710-940 t)

verdicts.limitation: One fresh seed per size; did not check the introduction position, so the 256^2 failure may be a failed establishment rather than a size effect; time series sampled every 4 t.
